title: Influence of Particle and Transport Effects on 231Pa/230Th Sensitivity to AMOC Changes
content:
Abstract

The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a critical driver of global climate variability on centennial to multi-millennial timescales, yet its past variability remains under-constrained. The sedimentary protactinium-to-thorium ratio (231Pa/230Th) is widely used to reconstruct past AMOC changes, but its interpretation is complicated by the influence of both large-scale circulation patterns and particle effects, leading to spatially heterogeneous responses. Here, we investigate the sensitivity of Atlantic 231Pa/230Th to idealized step-changes in AMOC strength in the Bern3D Earth system model across three different background climate states: the pre-industrial, the Last Glacial Maximum, and Marine Isotope Stage 3. By decomposing the 231Pa and 230Th responses into transport-driven and particle-induced components, we distinguish the primary influences on 231Pa/230Th in each experiment. We find that 231Pa/230Th is sensitive to AMOC changes, but the response depends on location, background climate, and circulation strength. Transport-dominated regions exhibit more consistent 231Pa/230Th responses across climate states, whereas particle-dominated regions show a less consistent response. Our results provide a framework for interpreting sedimentary 231Pa/230Th records and identifying regions where the proxy most robustly reflects AMOC variability. Models with higher spatial resolution and that better reproduce water column and sediment data will be essential to confirm and refine these findings.
